newsitem.title: UK: Cuban sugar output could reach 6.0 mln t by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Cuban sugar output could reach 6.0 mln t by 1999.

text.p: Cuba's sugar production could reach six million tonnes in the next two to three years, almost double the dismal 3.3 million turned out in 1994/95, the president of Cuba's state sugar trading firm Cubazucar said.

In an article for German statistician F.O. Licht's 1996/97 Sugar and Sweetener Yearbook, Alberto Betancourt said Cuba's sugar production in 1995/96 fell just 55,000 tonnes short of the official target of 4.5 million tonnes.

"As for the allocations to markets for the increasing availabilities, our problems up to the moment have tended to be marked by the lack of enough sugar to cover all the requirements from our potential customers," Betancourt said.
"We expect this to remain the case even with the increased production that we are counting on for the next two to three years, which could reach total levels of around six million tonnes."
Betancourt said the financing schemes in place to modernise Cuba's sugar industry gave grounds to expect a recovery which would not be limited to current crop results.

According to data from the International Sugar Organization (ISO), Cuba exported 3.67 million tonnes of sugar in the first six months of 1996, mainly to Russia, China and also lesser amounts to Morocco and Romania.
Exports for the first half of 1995 totalled 2.42 million tonnes, the ISO data showed.
